items.title: When everything is gone, where do families start again?
items.summary: When the Bhotekoshi River flash-flooded on the morning of August 26, families mainly in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts had little time to run and no time to save anything. items.title: Floods wash away 1,806 hectares of farmland, threaten food supplies

items.title: Nepal moves against online abuse targeting flood survivors

items.summary: Residents of Aamachhodingmo Rural Municipality who have lost family members look up for help when they hear a helicopter fly. Their prayers mostly go unanswered.

items.title: Flood sends hydropower shares tumbling, but damage is uneven
items.summary: The Bhotekoshi floods have hit a handful of listed hydropower projects, yet shares across the sector, and in insurance, have fallen as investors grapple with uncertainty over losses, claims and reconstruction.

items.title: Reporter’s Diary: I went back to Rasuwa. The river had changed everything
items.summary: Fourteen months after covering the first Lhende Khola flood, I returned to the same disaster zone. This time, roads and homes were gone, families were searching for their loved ones, and the places I remembered were barely recognisable.

items.title: Late rescues renew hope for survivors in deadly Nepal floods
items.summary: A 64-year-old woman was rescued alive from beneath her buried home as her family performed her death rites, while three others—including a Chinese national—were pulled alive from hydropower tunnels in Rasuwa.
